example_prompt: Handle Bictorys payment webhook notifications to automatically confirm orders when a payment succeeds.

input_schema.description: Payload Bictorys POSTs to your webhook URL when a payment event occurs.

id.description: Unique transaction identifier. Pass to verify_transaction for server-side confirmation.

phone.description: Digits only, no + prefix. Observed live: "33665909237".

amount.description: Amount paid by the customer in the stated currency.

settledAmount.description: Amount received after currency conversion, in settledCurrency.

paymentReference.description: Your paymentReference from create_charge. Use this to match the webhook to your order.

merchantReference.description: Your merchantReference from create_charge, if provided.

orderType.description: Origin of the charge: invoice, paymentlink, flat, order.

orderId.description: Associated invoice, order, or payment link identifier.

orderDetails.description: Line items if the charge included an itemized order.

status.description: Payment outcome, lowercase — same casing as verify_transaction. succeeded = paid; failed / cancelled = not paid; reversed = refunded/reversed; authorized = pre-authorized, not yet captured. "pending" and "processing" are intermediate states surfaced by verify_transaction polling, not delivered via this webhook.

timestamp.description: Transaction creation timestamp. NOT strict ISO 8601 — observed live format is "2026-08-08 18:45:44.10254" (space separator, no timezone, non-standard fractional-second digit count). Parse defensively; do not assume Date-constructor-safe ISO input.

response_schema.description: Your endpoint must return HTTP 200. The response body is ignored by Bictorys.

gotchas: Bictorys sends exactly ONE validation header: X-Secret-Key, containing the raw webhook secret you configured in the dashboard. There is no HMAC signature and no timestamp — neither X-Webhook-Signature nor X-Webhook-Timestamp is ever sent, and neither appears in Bictorys' documentation (https://docs.bictorys.com/docs/how-to-validate-webhooks). This header proves the sender knows the secret and says nothing about the body, so a tampered payload passes — measured: an amount rewritten from 100 to 100000 is accepted.

Because X-Secret-Key carries the secret in CLEAR on every delivery, never point a Bictorys webhook at a public capture bin (webhook.site, requestbin) using your real secret — anyone holding the bin URL can read it. Use a throwaway secret for capture testing, then rotate.

Since the header proves nothing about the body, the amount/currency/status/paymentReference cross-check below is not a belt-and-braces extra: it is the ONLY thing standing between you and a forged payload. Bictorys' own documentation presents it as a required step.
Always use crypto.timingSafeEqual() when comparing X-Secret-Key or HMAC values — never use === or ==. String equality comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks.
Bictorys retries the webhook up to 3 times if your endpoint returns a non-2xx status. Always respond HTTP 200 immediately, even if your internal processing fails — then handle errors asynchronously.

Express users: mount express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }) before express.json() on the webhook route, or keep req.rawBody. The raw body is what you log for audit, and what you would need if Bictorys ever adds a body signature; JSON.parse() loses it.

Don't gate fulfillment on an extra synchronous call to verify_transaction — a signature-verified webhook (HMAC or X-Secret-Key) combined with the anti-fraud amount/currency match below is already sufficient proof. verify_transaction's /status endpoint is known to be intermittently unavailable (see its own gotchas), so calling it here risks losing an already-successful payment to a transient outage on Bictorys' side. Reserve verify_transaction for the client-side redirect flow (which IS spoofable and needs it) and for reconciliation if a webhook never arrives.

Anti-fraud check: before fulfilling, verify that the webhook's amount and currency match your own order records — a forged or replayed payload could otherwise pass signature checks with tampered amounts.

Log the raw webhook payload to a persistent store (DB table) immediately after signature verification and before any business logic runs — this gives you an audit trail even if downstream processing fails, and is the natural place to implement the idempotency check above.
Implement idempotency using the transaction id field. Bictorys may deliver the same webhook event more than once; processing the same id twice must not double-fulfill an order.
Your webhook URL must be publicly reachable over HTTPS. Webhook configuration is separate for test vs. production environments in the Bictorys dashboard.

Bictorys recommends this webhook for apps with a backend server. For backend-less apps (e.g. static/mobile-only clients that can't expose a webhook endpoint), poll verify_transaction instead to check payment status.

The timestamp field is not strict ISO 8601 (space instead of 'T', no timezone, non-standard fractional-second precision — e.g. "2026-08-08 18:45:44.10254"). Don't rely on a strict ISO parser; use a lenient date library or normalize the string first.
